title: Putin, war leader and election campaign chief, prepares Russia for military escalation
subhead: For the first time since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Russians will elect their MPs between September 18 and 20. Orchestrated by the Kremlin, this vote carries no real electoral stakes and serves above all as a tool to rally support for the war effort.

title: Netanyahu orders evacuation of some West Bank settler outposts
subhead: In response to increased US pressure, Israeli's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered the evacuation of certain settlements in the occupied West Bank that were established without government approval.

title: Down with sexual laziness! Why sex is worth putting in the effort
subhead: Amid a growing trend of 'dating fatigue' and an increasing aversion to making an effort sexually, Le Monde's sex columnist Maïa Mazaurette explains how taking the easy way out leads nowhere when it comes to pleasure.

title: 'China will not replace the United States as a global power'
subhead: Dan Wang, a Chinese-Canadian researcher living in the US, has devoted his latest book, 'Breakneck: China's Quest to Engineer the Future,' to the two rival powers. In an interview with Le Monde, he discussed what sets them apart, but also what brings them together.

title: French left renews push to raise inheritance taxes, from forced philanthropy to wealth transfer cap
subhead: From the CFDT trade union to presidential candidates Raphaël Glucksmann and Marine Tondelier, the idea of increasing inheritance taxes is back on the table. The far-right Rassemblement National opposes it. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is considering another option: compulsory philanthropy for large inheritances.

title: Frida Kahlo's paintings, the wealthy collector and her cunning friend spark a fight for Mexico's art
subhead: On September 8, part of the most important collection of modern Mexican art assembled by Jacques and Natasha Gelman will be exhibited in Spain. The future of this priceless collection now lies with the Spanish bank Santander. In Mexico, a collective fears that these paintings, considered national heritage, may never be displayed in their home country again.
